name: DEM L316A (Hubble)
blurb: DEM L316A, the remnant of a supernova in the Large Magellanic Cloud, seen by Hubble.
label: deml316a-hubble
story: These rippling wisps of gas are what remains of a star that exploded long ago. Astronomers think the blast was a Type Ia supernova, set off when a white dwarf took on more matter from a companion than it could hold.

claims.text: DEM L316A is a supernova remnant (wisps of ionized gas)
It lies in the Large Magellanic Cloud
It formed in a Type Ia supernova
Type Ia: a white dwarf takes more material than it can handle from a companion
